title: Legal-hold aware retention webhook gateway and subscription manager
creator: Asha Raman
description: Implement a new webhook gateway + subscription manager that is aware of legal holds and retention suspension. Customers must be able to: 1) subscribe endpoints to receive legal-hold lifecycle events (create/update/release), residency-affecting toggles, and retention-change notifications; 2) query current hold state for a tenant and object keys; 3) ensure retention deletes are automatically suspended while a legal hold is active; and 4) receive verifiable, idempotent event delivery with audit metadata and replay support. This ticket covers the API shape, gateway implementation, idempotency/ack semantics, and migration plan for existing webhook subscribers.
acceptance_criteria: Public REST API endpoint to create/delete/inspect legal holds for tenant-level and object-level scopes
Subscription API allowing webhook endpoints to register for event types: legal_hold.created, legal_hold.updated, legal_hold.released, retention.policy.changed, residency.residency_toggled
Gateway guarantees at-least-once delivery with per-delivery idempotency key and long-term replay window (30 days) documented
Retention worker respects legal holds: any pending delete/ttl cleanup must be paused if a legal hold exists for the dataset/object

Event payloads include: hold_id, scope, reason, created_by, created_at, region_impact (list), retention_policy_snapshot, evidence_refs (links to audit doc/Drive), and a signed envelope for verification
Backward compatible for existing webhook subscribers: old contract still accepted; new fields optional
End-to-end tests including multi-region legal hold activation and subsequent abort of a scheduled delete
Monitoring dashboards for failed deliveries, avg retries to success, and percentage of retention actions suspended due to holds
implementation_notes: API: /v1/tenants/{tid}/legal_holds and /v1/objects/{oid}/legal_holds; PUT creates, PATCH updates, DELETE releases; GET returns active holds and history
Event routing: subscribe endpoints stored with per-event-type filters and optional region_scoping; gateway will honor rate limits and backoff window
Delivery semantics: initial attempt + exponential backoff, persist events to delivery-queue (kafka topic per-tenant) and mark delivery attempts with status codes and last_attempt_at
Idempotency: use event_id + delivery_attempt_id; require consumer to include X-Ack header; if ack missing, retry
Signature: HMAC-SHA256 using tenant-specific webhook secret stored in KMS; include signature header X-Redwood-Signature
Retention worker change: check legal_hold index (fast lookup) before executing delete job; if hold found, set job state to SUSPENDED and emit retention.suspended event
Evidence linking: when legal hold is created via API, accept optional evidence_url(s). Persist to audit store and include references in events for downstream legal teams
Data residency: when hold scope includes region constraints, mark affected regions and ensure retention suppression happens only where applicable
tradeoffs_and_decisions: At-least-once delivery chosen over exactly-once because it simplifies cross-region retries and persistence; idempotency keys are mandatory to protect consumers

We will not attempt synchronous confirmation from retention worker when creating a hold (avoid tight coupling). Instead, create hold in authoritative store and emit event; retention workers will observe and pick up changes within 10s window
Replay window set to 30 days to balance storage cost and customer need for audit replays; archive older events to cold storage with a note in the API
Signature verification uses HMAC with tenant-stored secret vs public-key verification to avoid PK rotation complexity in initial rollout. Evaluate PK approach in follow-up
Rate limiting: per-tenant per-endpoint; we will add batching and compressed payloads if customers need higher throughput
migration_plan: Phase 1 (read-only): deploy API and gateway in shadow mode for 2 weeks, emitting events to new topic but not altering retention behavior
Phase 2 (opt-in): allow customers to opt into legal-hold enforcement via tenant flag in console; collect feedback and fix issues
Phase 3 (enforced): enable enforcement for all tenants after 6 weeks and run migration script to reconcile any pending deletes against newly created holds
Rollback strategy: disable enforcement flag and replay release events to restore normal retention pipeline
testing_plan: Unit tests for API validation, signature generation/verification, and idempotency handling
Integration tests: create hold -> schedule delete -> verify delete suspended -> release hold -> verify delete proceeds
Chaos testing: simulate webhook endpoint flapping and high-latency delivery to ensure queue retention and replay work
Performance benchmark: delivery throughput target 2000 events/s per region with median 95th percentile delivery latency < 2s for local subscribers
Security tests: secret rotation, signature fuzzing, and event tamper detection
monitoring_and_diagnostics: New dashboards: 'Legal Hold Events Ingest', 'Webhook Delivery Success Rate', 'Retention Suspended Jobs'
Alerts: webhook delivery failure rate >5% sustained for 10m, retention job backlog increasing by >50% in 15m
Audit trail: every API call and event emission writes an immutable audit record (with region metadata) into the compliance-ledger bucket
Debug endpoints: /internal/debug/hold-lookup?tid={tid}&oid={oid} (RBAC restricted) for SRE/SE debugging
security_and_compliance: Secrets stored in customer KMS when available; otherwise in internal KMS with strict ACLs
All webhook payloads encrypted in transit (TLS) and signed. Payload bodies are not stored in plaintext beyond retention for the replay window
Design reviewed by Legal and Security on 2025-02-25 (notes: link to Confluence)
Retention suspension must be logged with operator id and justification for auditability
updates: 2025-02-18 - Asha Raman created ticket. Initial scoping and API sketch completed. Raised dependency on retention worker changes (ENG-27654).
2025-02-21 - Architecture sync with SRE and Security. Agreed on HMAC signatures and at-least-once delivery. Action: Marco to prototype gateway persistence layer.
2025-02-25 - Legal and Security review performed. Legal requested evidence_url field and immutable audit entries. Security requested KMS integration and a follow-up PK-based signature evaluation.

2025-02-28 - Prototype implemented: event persisted to kafka topic and delivered to mock subscriber. Early integration test showed retention worker picks up hold within 8s. Found an edge case where multi-tenant queue ordering caused a short-lived false-positive delete; created sub-issue ENG-72112 to address ordering by shard.
2025-03-03 - UX/PM reviewed subscription API. Requested add 'region_scope' parameter and clearer retry headers for consumers. Added to implementation_notes.
2025-03-05 - Began writing integration tests and adding monitoring dashboards. Assigned Marco as owner for rollout coordination.
